## Problem Statement

New users face a blank platform: the first workbench, first pipeline, and first
model deployment all start from empty forms, and time-to-first-success is
measured in days. We want a curated tutorial gallery in the Dashboard — a set
of maintained, tested tutorials (notebooks and pipelines) that users can launch
into their own project with one click. This requires product code (the gallery
and launch mechanics), authored content (the tutorials themselves), and
documentation — three different kinds of work with different owners and review
processes.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook, or importing the pipeline). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment, first RAG app. Each is tested against the current release. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution process for new tutorials. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Notebooks
- Data Science Pipelines
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Partner- or community-contributed tutorial intake (contribution process is
  documented, but no submission tooling this release)
- Localization of tutorial content

## Open Questions

None.

# Tutorial packaging format and validation tooling

## Description

Defines the tutorial packaging format that decouples tutorial content from
Dashboard releases, plus the tooling that validates a packaged tutorial against
it. The format is the contract that both the Dashboard tutorial gallery (which
reads tutorial metadata and launches pinned images) and authored tutorial
content (which is packaged, versioned, and tested in the format) build against.
This epic's priority is P0 by priority inheritance: it directly gates both P0
requirements of the strategy (the gallery launch mechanics and the curated
tutorial suite).

## Scope

- Define the tutorial packaging format: a metadata descriptor per tutorial
  (identity, covered journey, tutorial kind — notebook or pipeline), pinned
  container images, and a validation manifest.
- Define the versioning scheme that lets a tutorial package be released and
  updated independently of Dashboard releases.
- Provide validation tooling that mechanically checks a packaged tutorial
  conforms to the format (metadata completeness, image pinning, manifest
  present and consistent).
- The format spans Dashboard, Notebooks, and Data Science Pipelines surfaces;
  this epic is assigned to the Dashboard component because the gallery is the
  primary consumer, and is owned by the Dashboard team with review from the
  Workbenches and Pipelines teams as the other format consumers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The format specification documents the metadata fields, image pinning rules,
  and validation manifest structure.
- A tutorial packaged in the format can be validated mechanically with a
  pass/fail result by the validation tooling.
- A versioned tutorial package can be updated to a new version without
  requiring a Dashboard release.
- The format specification is reviewed and agreed by the Dashboard, Workbenches,
  and Pipelines teams (all three consuming teams).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): a tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation
  manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of
  Dashboard releases. Epic priority is P0 by inheritance — this format gates
  the P0 gallery and P0 tutorial suite work.

# Dashboard tutorial gallery and one-click launch

## Description

Adds the tutorial gallery to the Dashboard: a curated, browsable set of
tutorials that a user can launch into their own project with one click —
opening a workbench pre-loaded with the tutorial notebook, or importing the
tutorial pipeline into the project's Data Science Pipelines instance. The
gallery reads tutorial packages conforming to the defined tutorial packaging
format.

## Scope

- Gallery surface in the Dashboard listing available tutorial packages, driven
  by the packaging format's metadata (journey, kind, version).
- One-click launch mechanics for notebook tutorials: create/open a workbench in
  the user's selected project with the tutorial notebook loaded, using the
  pinned image from the tutorial package.
- One-click launch mechanics for pipeline tutorials: import the packaged
  pipeline into the project's Data Science Pipelines instance.
- Configuration/feature-flag wiring following existing Dashboard conventions
  (OdhDashboardConfig).
- Incidental gallery UI text and captions that fall out of this change are
  included here as scope; they are not separately authored content.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user can browse the tutorial gallery in the Dashboard and see the available
  tutorials with their metadata.
- Launching a notebook tutorial creates or opens a workbench in the user's
  project with the tutorial notebook loaded and the pinned image running.
- Launching a pipeline tutorial imports the pipeline into the project's Data
  Science Pipelines instance.
- End-to-end launch is verified against a tutorial package conforming to the
  defined packaging format (both tutorial kinds).
- The gallery renders and launches correctly for a user with a single selected
  project, with resources landing in that project.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): the Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch
  a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook, or
  importing the pipeline).

# Curated notebook tutorial suite

## Description

Authors the five notebook-based tutorials covering the core getting-started
journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run, first deployment, and
first RAG app. Each tutorial is packaged in the defined tutorial packaging
format and tested end-to-end against the current release. This epic is content
authoring (curated sample notebooks), not platform code: the workbench,
training, serving, and RAG surfaces it exercises are existing, generally
available platform capabilities.

## Scope

- Author five notebook tutorials: first workbench, data prep, first training
  run, first deployment, first RAG app.
- Package each tutorial per the tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned
  images, validation manifest).
- Test each tutorial end-to-end against the current release: the workbench
  starts in a user project and the notebook runs to completion.
- The tutorials exercise workbench, training, model serving, and RAG surfaces;
  the single most-relevant canonical component is Notebooks (the tutorials are
  notebook content running on workbenches). No code changes to the notebook
  platform itself — the existing workbench lifecycle is used as-is.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All five notebook tutorials exist and are packaged in the defined tutorial
  packaging format.
- Each tutorial passes the format's validation tooling.
- Each tutorial has been executed end-to-end against the current release in a
  user project (workbench starts, notebook runs to completion).
- Tutorial content is technically reviewed for accuracy against current
  platform behavior.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): six curated tutorials covering the core journeys, each tested
  against the current release — this epic covers the five notebook journeys;
  the first-pipeline journey is authored by the Pipelines team as a separate
  unit of work.

# Tutorial gallery documentation

## Description

Documentation for the tutorial gallery: how users browse the gallery and launch
tutorials into their own projects, and the contribution process for authoring
and submitting new tutorials against the packaging format. This is Red Hat
docs content work using the docs content process and tooling.

## Scope

Content outline (authored topics):

- Getting started with the tutorial gallery — what it is, where to find it, and
  what a tutorial launches into the user's project.
- Launching your first tutorial — the notebook flow (workbench opens with the
  notebook) and the pipeline flow (pipeline import), including how to pick a
  project.
- Contributing a tutorial — the packaging format reference (metadata, pinned
  images, validation manifest), how to validate a package, and the submission
  process for new tutorials. Per the strategy's out-of-scope statement, the
  contribution process is documented but no submission tooling is delivered
  this release; the docs describe the documented intake path only.
- No localization of tutorial content (out of scope per strategy).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation covers using the gallery: browsing tutorials and launching
  both tutorial kinds (notebook and pipeline) into a project.
- Documentation covers the contribution process for new tutorials, including
  the packaging format and validation steps.
- Content is technically reviewed against the implemented gallery and the
  delivered tutorials — steps match current release behavior.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution
  process for new tutorials. Epic priority is P1 per the docs-authoring
  priority exception (strategy frontmatter priority Major → P1).
